title: Planar STL boundary extraction and Gmsh 2D generation
overview: Reads a triangulated STL region in the XY plane, reconstructs one closed boundary loop, assigns named boundary groups from a JSON sidecar, and writes Gmsh geometry. Gmsh remains an optional external executable.
principle: STL facets carry coordinates and triangle topology, not standard CFD boundary-condition semantics. Singly incident triangle edges form the outer boundary; a sidecar explicitly maps every boundary edge to a named Gmsh Physical Curve. Physical names require a separate mapping to OneFLOW BC semantics.
architecture: ASCII/Binary STL -> vertex welding and XY topology validation -> single closed boundary loop -> sidecar edge-to-physical-name mapping -> Gmsh .geo -> optional Gmsh CLI -> MSH -> existing Gmsh import and CGNS conversion path.

proves: ASCII and binary STL triangle records can be read and a planar square fixture yields one four-edge boundary loop.
Every outer edge can be assigned to a named Gmsh Physical Curve and the generated geometry can request one quadrilateral cell.
does_not_prove: Gmsh CLI has been executed or the emitted MSH contains exactly one quadrilateral element.
Generated MSH has been converted through CGNS into a OneFLOW native grid.
Boundary names are automatically translated into OneFLOW solver boundary-condition types.
Arbitrary plane orientations, holes, multiple components, curved reconstruction or general multi-cell meshing are supported.
